basis: Progressive muscular dystrophy; borderline intellectual disability in 2/2 patients supports neurologic involvement.
Congenital skeletal myopathy, including respiratory muscles; muscle weakness does not establish intrinsic pulmonary damage. Cardiac findings occur in <30%.
Hypogonadotropic hypogonadism; dental abnormalities and osteopenia each reported in 2/5 patients (40%). Hearing impairment 20%; anosmia frequency unspecified.
Cerebellar degeneration, neuropathy and vestibular failure define disease; supplied HPO reports optic atrophy and joint contractures each in 30-79%, although atypical for classic CANVAS.
Intellectual disability and skeletal anomalies define syndrome; heart defects ~40-50% and dental anomalies >30%. Qualifying ocular findings omitted at four-axis cap.
Severe congenital hypomyelinating neuropathy and multiple joint contractures define syndrome; respiratory paralysis does not establish intrinsic lung injury.
Tumor originates in small intestinal mucosa; neuroendocrine differentiation alone does not establish endocrine gland disease or a hormonal disorder.
Microcephaly, seizures and developmental impairment define syndrome; camptodactyly/brachydactyly and hydronephrosis each annotated in 30-79%. Genital hypoplasia lacks endocrine evidence.
Lymphoid malignancy involving urinary bladder; bladder belongs to renal axis, and lymphoma warrants hematologic and immune mechanism axes.
Endocardial fibrosis causes cardiomyopathy and cardiac failure. Syndromic endocrine and neurologic HPO findings are not established features of this broad cardiac concept.
Malignant peripheral nerve sheath tumor arising from cutaneous nerves; nerve origin establishes neurologic axis. Metastatic organ involvement is not assumed.
Myosin storage skeletal myopathy; hypertrophic cardiomyopathy in 3/3 and heart failure in 2/3 patients. Restrictive ventilation may reflect muscle/chest-wall disease.
Primary immunodeficiency defined by deficient number or function of circulating NK lymphocytes; no specific secondary organ damage established.
Hydranencephaly and congenital diaphragm defect define syndrome; pulmonary hypoplasia is common (>30%) with lethal diaphragmatic hernia. Cardiac anomaly frequency unspecified.
Immune attack with defining skin sclerosis and oral lesions; damaging ocular dryness affects ~40-60%. Hepatic and pulmonary involvement omitted at four-axis cap.
Severe obesity with insulin resistance defines metabolic disease; speech/language developmental impairment is annotated in 30-79%, supporting neurologic involvement.
Defining ocular malformations, valvular heart disease, skeletal deformities and muscle hypoplasia. Ear shape and palate findings alone do not establish additional organ dysfunction.
Subcutaneous lipomas and limb hemihyperplasia define syndrome; cerebral vascular malformations annotated in 30-79%. Renal enlargement <30%; embryonal tumors are a later risk.
Mullerian duct aplasia affects reproductive structures outside the axes; renal or skeletal abnormalities are not established across this umbrella concept.
Phenylalanine metabolic disorder; cognitive impairment, seizures and developmental dysfunction are defining manifestations of untreated disease, commonly >30%.
Coexisting Hodgkin and non-Hodgkin lymphoid malignancies; no particular extranodal organ is specified.
Immune-mediated inflammatory bowel disease directly damages intestinal tissue; no common intrinsic extraintestinal organ damage established for this subtype.
Inherited cardiac electrical dysfunction causing arrhythmias; syncope does not establish independent neurologic injury.
In situ carcinoma originates in breast ducts; breast has no axis, and apocrine differentiation does not make this a skin or endocrine disease.
Structural anomalies and cysts of the iris pigment epithelium are confined to the eye.
